Reward sensitivity?

A large-scale study of 6-to-10-year-old children (Coley, 2012) found that engaging in activities related to "exploring nature" was associated with making more ecological inferences (i.e., generalizing a novel property to a dissimilar but ecologically related species). Coley also found that the (adult) tendency to make ecological inferences for diseases and taxonomic inferences for insides emerges earlier in rural children than in urban children.
